origin.description: Construct one piece of a pillar: a length-one list plus a width and a minimum width.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A bare list of length one. The element is the contents of the component.

arguments.name: width, min_width
arguments.text: Width and minimum width. Both are one integer-valued number. If min_width is NULL, it matches width.

origin.details: The object is that list, with width and min_width stored as integers and class pillar_component. width has to be named, because it follows the empty dots. A whole number such as 1.0 is accepted and stored as an integer. letters[1:3] at width 1 keeps a, b, and c, with minimum width 1.

translation.description: The same list and the same two integers. None for a width is a missing integer.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A list of length one. A string or a subclass of list is rejected.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: One integer-valued number, passed by name. 1.0 is stored as 1. A bool, a fraction, and a number past 2^52 are rejected.

arguments.name: min_width
arguments.text: One integer-valued number. None uses width.

translation.details: The component keeps a copy of the outer list. Both widths are Python ints, or None when R would store NA. Inf warns and becomes None. NaN becomes None without a warning. An extra positional or keyword is an error, and the message is the check_dots_empty text, including the note about naming an argument.
translation.value: A pillar_component with x, width, and min_width.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.num_colors": 8, "cli.unicode": True})

from pillar.parts import new_pillar_component

print(new_pillar_component([["a", "b", "c"]], width=1))
